item.text: I’m checking whether the 2024 social-service side was run through competent technocrats or patronage channels, starting with IMF, World Bank, ministry, and Reuters material, then I’ll stop and synthesize the strongest claim-level evidence.

item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mixed, leaning negative. There is real technocratic evidence in the finance/budget chain and the education reform package, but the state still showed weak execution, salary-heavy social budgets, and repeated independent criticism that resources were squandered and services stayed underfunded.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Democratic Republic of Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes) | World Bank | 2024-02-28 | The PEQIP education project explicitly pushed merit-based teacher recruitment, more qualified female teachers, better classroom materials, stronger information systems, decentralized planning, and support for students with disabilities. This is solid evidence that at least part of the social-services apparatus was being designed with competence and professional management in mind. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- [Democratic Republic of Congo: 2024 Article IV Consultation, Sixth Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr) | IMF | 2024-07-03 | The IMF said the authorities cleaned up the civil-service register using biometric identification, reorganized civil-service social security coverage, and launched a retirement program, while also saying a broader civil-service reform was still needed. This supports a limited competence-first reading, but not a fully resolved one. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`

- [Deux Nouveaux programmes avec le FMI : Aimé BOJI et Doudou Fwamba étaient devant la presse.](https://budget.gouv.cd/deux-nouveaux-programmes-avec-le-fmi-aime-boji-et-doudou-fwamba-etaient-devant-la-presse/) | Ministère du Budget | 2024-11-15 | The budget ministry said the Finance and Budget ministers jointly negotiated the new IMF programs and credited improved coordination between the ministries since June 2024, with transparency in public-finance management cited as a key reform driver. This is one of the clearest favorable signs that social-service funding was being handled through professional fiscal channels rather than purely patronage politics. | IDs: `6B.4`, `5B.10`

- [Profil du Ministre des Finances](https://adminfinances.cd/ProfilMin.php) | Administration des Finances | 2024 | Doudou Fwamba is presented as a career finance official with economics and public-finance training, more than ten years inside the ministry, and experience on reform projects. That is direct evidence that Tshisekedi placed a competent professional in a key finance role relevant to social-service funding. | IDs: `6B.4`, `5B.10`

- [Strengthening Public Social Spending in DRC](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/227/article-A002-en.xml) | IMF | 2024 | The IMF said social spending had risen and education and health were prioritized, but it also found that social budgets were credibility-poor, salary-heavy, and badly executed, with very low implementation of domestically financed investment. This is strong mixed evidence, but the execution side weighs against a clean competence-first finding. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`

- [DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said public resources were squandered, leaving essential services underfunded and harming food, healthcare, water, sanitation, education, and housing. That is strong negative evidence that social services were not being managed with consistent professional competence. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- [DRC: President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | Amnesty said the humanitarian response remained chronically underfunded and that the state of siege militarized everyday life, with urgent needs for shelter, food, healthcare, and education still unmet. That points to social-service governance being subordinated to coercive and political priorities rather than competent service delivery. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- [DR Congo second term should focus rights](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/dr-congo-second-term-should-focus-rights) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-06 | HRW said corruption and repression reduced the government’s capacity to deliver quality education, healthcare, and social security, and that systemic reform was lagging. This is strong negative evidence against a genuinely professional, depoliticized social-service apparatus. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Search Gap**
- I found good evidence on education, fiscal coordination, and some civil-service reform, but not a full audit of health, welfare, or local-service staffing quality in 2024.
- Direct evidence on whether patronage networks still dominated line ministries is thinner than the indirect evidence from IMF/NGO execution criticism.
- The best-supported conclusion is that Tshisekedi mixed some technocratic appointments and reform talk with a system that still underperformed badly in social-service delivery.
